# Phase 1 assessment: test case design

## Evidence reviewed

- Pinned story (`user_story`, `characters 0-16000`): Python 3.12, Flask, server-rendered password-reset exercise with pytest, synthetic accounts, in-memory notifications, production-limitations documentation, and no deployment or deployment workflows.
- Supplied image (`attachment`, `457acc5e-8bce-44d6-abec-d204c28e4d84`, `sign-in-wireframe.png`): a white page with a centered bordered sign-in panel; bold "Sign in" heading; stacked, labeled "Email address" and "Password" inputs with `name@example.com` and masked `********` placeholders; blue underlined "Forgot password?" link beneath password; wide dark "Sign in" button; muted "No account? Contact your administrator." footer. The image does not prove working interactions, a recovery-page design, exact CSS values, or sign-in success behavior. The attachment reader supplies the reference, while these visual observations come from the image supplied with the task.
- Curated account recovery standard (`knowledge`, `28e06fb4-ccd1-4117-8f7b-b2a6c9bfaf1f`, `v1, chunk 0`): account-independent request response; at most five requests per account per hour; single-use links expiring 30 minutes after issue; all active sessions signed out and owner notified after each successful reset.
- Approved `requirements_analysis`: REQ-001 through REQ-018 and their acceptance criteria. Approved `ui_analysis`: observed sign-in properties distinguished from proposed recovery and accessibility states. Approved `solution_design`: TASK-001 through TASK-006, their acceptance criteria, architecture, and an empty `coverage_dispositions` list. Approved `acceptance_20261028191242_8eaf7f_risk`: six prospective verification risks linked across all 18 requirements. The prior-output reader supplied stage keys but no citation locators; cite original evidence references above in the output rather than inventing stage-output locators.

## Coverage and design implications

Every approved requirement has at least one solution-design task: TASK-001 covers REQ-001/002/013/014; TASK-002 covers REQ-009/011/012; TASK-003 covers REQ-003/004/005; TASK-004 covers REQ-006/007/008/009/010; TASK-005 covers REQ-015; TASK-006 covers REQ-016/017/018. Each individual acceptance criterion needs a proposed test with a stable TC-NNN ID, concrete observable expected result, requirement and task links, preconditions and data incorporated into the available contract fields, and appropriate original-evidence references. Since the solution design records no justified non-test dispositions, plan for test coverage of every REQ-001 through REQ-018; treat the no-deployment requirements as delivery-action and repository-change inspections, not application runtime tests.

Include positive, negative, and boundary scenarios: sign-in presentation and recovery navigation; valid existing versus unknown versus at-limit public response equality; five accepted requests, sixth refusal, and rolling-hour boundary with private sink inspection; token GET versus POST, wrong-account isolation, malformed/replayed links, a request that expires while its form is open, the instant before and exactly at 30 minutes, and competing submissions; password hash change, all previously active sessions rejected, and owner notice only for successful resets. Cover server rendering, synthetic/in-memory isolation, pytest test inventory, production-limitations documentation, and delivery scope. Check programmatic labels, keyboard/focus and error presentation for user-facing flows, without treating UI proposals as observed image facts. Avoid inventing sign-in authentication, precise recovery copy, password-complexity limits, or an external notification service.

## Gaps and questions

No implementation, test execution, deployment action log, or repository-change proof was supplied by these evidence tools: proposed tests cannot be reported as passing, and the negative delivery checks will require review of actual delivery evidence when available. Sign-in success and session creation, recovery-page wording/layout, password validation beyond nonempty input, and invalid-link presentation remain nonblocking open questions in approved predecessors. Test only approved behavior and label design-specific expectations as provisional; ask for a consequential decision before asserting any of these unspecified behaviors as a requirement.

Phase 1 stops with this assessment. No product documents or test results were produced.
